It was not that long ago that the Libertarian party was seen as an extreme left wing party that was not far from communism. Somewhere the message changed and we're seen as anarco-capitalists. We are, really, pretty far left but not extreme unless you compare us to the American Right Wing groups.

I am all for the legalization of all drugs for those who have reached the age of majority. I think we should end the war on drugs and use that money for treatment and education. I feel good paying my taxes but i wish they were spent more wisely - yet I do not begrudge a stupid spending spree or expensive projects that are really trivial compared to the overall budget. I like the idea of single payer health care and have been advocating for it for well over twenty years. (I'm 57, if you're confused.)

I sold my business, it was quite successful, and the parent company is an almost household name - they specialize in filling government contracts almost exclusively. Before I even had access to my money, from selling the business, I paid an eight figure sum in taxes. Yes, eight digits. It was expensive but, frankly, it was less than what I probably owed for what I gained. Today I pay a tiny percentage of my income in taxes - I pay a lower percentage than you do. (I pay much more than you do, probably.) My income is derived from capital gains. I am okay with that - I don't mind the taxes one bit. I am honored to pay them. And, trust me, it does not eat into my lifestyle one bit. I actually live pretty cheaply though I have an affinity for automobiles and property.

I guess the way my accountant described it is good. "You don't pay taxes any more on what you have. That's been taxed already. Think of it this way, in your case you pay taxes the minute you take it out of the bank - that's when it becomes income."

So, I pay a minimal amount of taxes (such is my obligation - I do all of the lawful tax avoidance methods that my accountant knows and tax avoidance is legal where tax evasion is illegal) and then I donate a bunch of money to projects and organizations I agree with. I've even sent NASA money. It is my belief that my luck has enabled me to be in a position where I am financially comfortable and that this situation was brought about by the society that rewarded me. It is my obligation to contribute back to that society. When I donate money, I view it as a tax with greater representation than I get from my real taxes. I view it as a requirement as it is a part of my social contract.

I say these things not out of some ego stroking attempt to get e-penis. I say them because I want you, and other readers, to know that not all those who use the Libertarian descriptor are monsters who are hell bent on anarcho-capitalism and working towards the lowest common denominator. It is my attempt at doing the responsible thing and providing education and awareness. It is my attempt to adjust the narrative to be more accurate.

At the same time, I acknowledge that the problems with the party stem from the party itself. I'm running for the Senate in my state and will be running under the Libertarian Party banner. I have a lot of work to do. However, I will never be a party leader nor do I want to. It would be like herding cats and some of them are malicious cats.

I am all for the legalization of all drugs for those who have reached the age of majority. I think we should end the war on drugs and use that money for treatment and education. I feel good paying my taxes but i wish they were spent more wisely - yet I do not begrudge a stupid spending spree or expensive projects that are really trivial compared to the overall budget. I like the idea of single payer health care and have been advocating for it for well over twenty years. (I'm 57, if you're confused.)

I sold my business, it was quite successful, and the parent company is an almost household name - they specialize in filling government contracts almost exclusively. Before I even had access to my money, from selling the business, I paid an eight figure sum in taxes. Yes, eight digits. It was expensive but, frankly, it was less than what I probably owed for what I gained. Today I pay a tiny percentage of my income in taxes - I pay a lower percentage than you do. (I pay much more than you do, probably.) My income is derived from capital gains. I am okay with that - I don't mind the taxes one bit. I am honored to pay them. And, trust me, it does not eat into my lifestyle one bit. I actually live pretty cheaply though I have an affinity for automobiles and property.

I guess the way my accountant described it is good. "You don't pay taxes any more on what you have. That's been taxed already. Think of it this way, in your case you pay taxes the minute you take it out of the bank - that's when it becomes income."

So, I pay a minimal amount of taxes (such is my obligation - I do all of the lawful tax avoidance methods that my accountant knows and tax avoidance is legal where tax evasion is illegal) and then I donate a bunch of money to projects and organizations I agree with. I've even sent NASA money. It is my belief that my luck has enabled me to be in a position where I am financially comfortable and that this situation was brought about by the society that rewarded me. It is my obligation to contribute back to that society. When I donate money, I view it as a tax with greater representation than I get from my real taxes. I view it as a requirement as it is a part of my social contract.

I say these things not out of some ego stroking attempt to get e-penis.
